text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- In a meeting with Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres in Washington, U.S. President Bill Clinton said the United States would pressure the U.N. in order to guarantee human rights in East Timor. The two leaders also discussed NATO and Africa.

- Parliament yesterday approved Portugal's participation in the U.N. Convention on the Law of the Sea. Health Minister Maria de Belem will sign today the European Council's Convention on Human Rights and Biomedicine.

- Portugal's association of canned food industries has written to the main political parties asking them to vote against ratification of a European Union law to liberalise imports of Moroccan canned fish to the EU. It said the law would harm the interests of Portugal's canned fish industry, the largest in Europe.
- Growth of the Portuguese banking sector is slowing down, according to a report from SaeR, a local ratings company.
- The government plans to charge people minimum and maximum income and corporate tax payments according to their job type.
- The cabinet is set to approve in May a European Union directive to preserve the environment in partnership with economic development.

- A controversial request by the Union of General Workers trade union group UGT for a state guarantee for its debts coincided with salary negotiations between the UGT and the government, Finance Minister Antonio de Sousa Franco and UGT leader Joao Proenca said yesterday.
- Ship repairer Lisnave posted 1996 losses of 5.5 billion escudos of losses, compared with losses of 9.6 billion in 1995.
- Portuguese trucking companies are losing 1.4 billion escudos a month in revenues due to restructions imposed by the Spanish government on the circulation of trucks on Sundays and public holidays.
